raw_response:
I farm 20 mu, and I do not spread money evenly just to look neat. I start from what has worked for me around Quzhou. Wheat and maize are still my main food-and-cash base because I have well water, so I will keep most land in the wheat-maize rotation. Stevia can bring cash, but it needs more watching, more hand work, and cleaner field management, so I will not put too much area into it. This year I will do 15 mu in wheat-maize rotation and 5 mu in stevia. For wheat, I will feed it a bit heavier because if wheat stools weak in winter or turns pale in spring, yield is hard to pull back. For maize, I will also keep fertilizer on the safe side because summer crop grows fast and I do not want empty tips. Since I have irrigation, I will use water at the key times instead of gambling on rain. Stevia is different from grain crops, so I will keep its area smaller, use more careful potassium, and manage weeds and insects more closely because leaf quality matters. I watch costs, but on 20 mu I still think losing yield is worse than spending a bit more on fertilizer, so I will stay close to what good growers around me do and only adjust a little where I see a clear reason.
